messages:
Alex M.: Heads-up — I'm leaving Redwood at the end of next month. Need advice: considering a 401(k) withdrawal for a house down payment vs rolling to an IRA. What happens tax/penalty-wise on separation? Any deadline/lock periods I should know about? @people-ops
Sara (People Ops): Congrats on the next step, Alex! :tada: Short version: you can either roll the balance to an IRA or your new employer's plan, or take a distribution. Rollovers avoid immediate taxes and withheld cash. Distributions are taxable and, if you're under 59½, typically subject to a 10% early-withdrawal penalty unless an exception applies.
Alex M.: Cool. Is there any company blackout where the admin holds funds after termination? I have an offer deadline for the house deposit and need exact timing.
Ben - Payroll: We don't hold funds. Once HR submits the termination payload, the plan admin starts processing. Typical flow: admin acknowledges within ~3–5 business days, then distribution/rollover completes in about 7–14 business days. Paper checks or mailed forms can add time.
Linda (Finance): Important: if you take a check payable to you, the plan must withhold 20% federal tax on eligible rollover distributions. For a direct rollover to an IRA, no withholding occurs. So for partial cash-outs, think about withholding and whether you'll need to make up withheld amounts to complete a 60-day rollover.
Alex M.: Can I do a partial distribution and roll the rest? I only need ~10k for the down payment.
Sara (People Ops): Most plans allow partial distributions, yes. We can pull the plan admin's distribution form. Confirm whether the plan requires a minimum residual balance if you leave some funds in the plan.
TaxBot: IRS note: if you separate from service in the year you turn 55 or later, distributions from that employer plan may avoid the 10% penalty. That doesn't apply if you're 33. Also the 60-day rollover window applies to indirect rollovers.
Alex M.: If I roll to a traditional IRA and then withdraw for the house, will I still face penalty/taxes?
Linda (Finance): Traditional IRA withdrawals before 59½ are generally taxable plus 10% penalty. Roth IRAs have contribution vs conversion rules; first-time homebuyer exception allows up to $10k of qualified distributions (Roth earnings exclusion conditions apply). Recommend a personal tax consultation for your timing and conversion strategy.
Ben - Payroll: Operational checklist: tell us direct rollover vs check payable to you, or partial. For direct rollover we need the receiving custodian name, account number, and EIN (or trustee-to-trustee transfer authorization).
Sara (People Ops): Action items: Alex — DM me which you want (partial cash-out + rollover vs full rollover). I'll request the admin forms and check for any upcoming admin maintenance/blackout windows this quarter. I'll also offer to schedule a quick call with the benefits vendor rep.
Alex M.: Please queue the forms and vendor call. Also confirm if there's any minimum waiting period after termination before the admin will approve a distribution.
Ben - Payroll: Will check and reply in-thread if there's any plan-specific delay. If the admin has a scheduled upgrade/maintenance we'll flag it and try to process before your termination date.
Sara (People Ops): Sent DM and flagged a benefits rep meeting option for Friday. We'll follow up with the distribution packet and estimated timeline. :email:
